html:
In July 1893 French gunboats forced their way past the forts at Paknam, at the mouth of the Chao Phraya, and anchored off Bangkok. Siam had to give up all its lands east of the Mekong to France.

France wanted Laos for French Indochina. Britain, which Siam had hoped would help, did not. King Chulalongkorn fell ill from the shock.

The losses became French Laos. Siam later ceded more lands in Cambodia and the Malay states, but kept its independence as a buffer between British and French empires, the only state in Southeast Asia never colonised.
